recipes.name: Chicken Fajita Melts
ingredients_raw: 6 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, thinly sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, and cook and stir until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the sliced onions and red peppers, and cook and stir for 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Stir in the tomato juice and taco seasoning, and mix well. Cook mixture until the juice has thickened and the chicken is well coated with sauce, about an additional 7 minutes.
Preheat the oven’s broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source.

Arrange French bread slices on a baking sheet. Spread 2 tablespoons of salsa over each slice of French bread. Evenly spoon the chicken mixture on top of the salsa topped bread. Sprinkle each sandwich with 1/4 cup Cheddar cheese.
Broil under the preheated broiler until the cheese is melted and beginning to brown, up to 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Fajita Melts
raw_recipe.description: These cheesy chicken fajita melts pile seasoned chicken, peppers, onions, salsa, and melted Cheddar onto thick slices of French bread for an easy family dinner.

video.description: Get that fajita flavor fast with this open-faced melt sandwich version of your favorite chicken fajitas! Cook chicken breast with onions and bell pepper, then stir in tomato juice and taco seasoning. Spread French bread with salsa, chicken mixture and cheddar cheese. Place it under a broiler until it gets toasty, melty and juicy, then sink your teeth in to great taste.

review.reviewBody: very good! I added sliced avocado and sliced tomatoes underneath the chicken mixture and added extra cheese. I also used rye bread which turned out yummy! One tip: toast the bread on both sides under the broiler so it won't get soggy when you add the toppings.

I absolutely love doing this recipe. I’ve made it several times and it’s turned out perfect every time. I actually use tomato sauce instead of tomato juice and I bake it all first to make the bread a little crunchy on the bottom. I also use the mini mixed peppers to add color and taste. Definitely one of my favorite recipes.

New family favorite. I didn't have bread on hand so I layered recipe in a 9x13. First chicken, veggies, sauce, cheese covered it and baked in 350* oven for 30 minutes covered 10 additional minutes uncovered. Also once I added 1/4 c ranch dressing to sauce. Yummy

Big pet peeve is people who change the recipe then rate it… well this time I’m guilty! I used the basic recipe but could not bring myself to put tomato juice in it… instead used a good beer (trust me)… I also used Fajita seasoning… after all you called it that. Last, I used a mix of “Mexican Blend” cheese and added some mozzarella. Came out amazing! Some tips though… cut chicken into strips and season with oil, lime, fajita seasoning and let it sit in fridge for about an hour or so to marinate. Pick a GOOD salsa, and we tried both plain Italian bread and garlic bread… 3 out of 4 all preferred the garlic bread MAINLY as it was cut thicker but both were good. Will make again

I made this with a couple changes. Didn’t have tomato juice so I used a can of Rotelle’s Fire Roasted flavor as a substitute. Also got fresh garlic bread and broiled both sides before piling on the good stuff on each piece. Topped with sour cream. Delish!!

I never change a recipe before I try the original, however I did not have bread worthy of a melt and no taco seasoning. I made the recipe according to direction subbing cumin and fajita season for taco season. (Put it on meat when browning too) I made some rice seasoned with cilantro and lime juice. Put the rice in a shallow baking dish and pour chicken mix over it, then the cheese. Very good, I must say! Next time I will make sure I have some nice bread on hand. Thanks for the recipe

Great and easy!! Don’t be intimidated by the tomato juice - it does work! And cooks down as you simmer. I used a 5oz can plus 1 TBLS of tomato paste I had leftover from another recipe. (Although I could see beer being good here too as another reviewer suggested). I only had a green bell pepper but it added a nice color contrast. Finally- I lightly toasted the bread under the broiler before adding the salsa, sliced avocado, chicken mix and cheese. Jalapeños or black olives could be fun here too. This was very good and a quick weeknight meal I would make again. Thanks laughingmagpie!

This was very good. I doubled the tomato sauce, and added crushed red pepper. I did grill the chicken but that is just personal preference. I sprinkled Mrs. Dash grilled chicken over the chicken while grilling.

This certainly is a different delicious way to enjoy chicken. I cooked my chicken almost all the way through first and removed from heat while the peppers and onion cooked. Then added chicken back in with the seasonings. I can see how easy it is to over cook the chicken.. Especially after the broiling. I added 2 cloves of garlic as well. I like the addition of avocado as another reviewer suggested, and will try that next time. Thanks for a simple quick yet still tasty dish.

This was delicious, however I did tweak the recipe a bit. Instead of using bread, I made Spanish rice then layered the rice then the chicken and veggies on top of the rice in a casserole dish. I then continued with the salsa and cheese, then under the broiler as the recipe says. My whole family LOVED it.

This was amazing! Of course, I made a couple of changes. After a long day, frozen veggies also worked for me. And following a reviewers comment, I sliced the French bread in half and made it open faced. Added a Mexican blend of cheeses and home made pico and guacamole. Will definitely make this again!

My family loves this recipe and I have some picky eaters. I don't add the salsa until they are cooked. I top each one with salsa and sour cream because some of my family members prefer it without salsa. I also bake it instead of broil so that the bread is crunchy. This is one of those recipes that stays in my mind. It's so easy and yet so flavorful and delicious. It's better than fajitas to me. Thank you!
My family loved it! It was simple to make and it was a big hit for a Saturday night dinner!!!!!
Came out great. I toasted the bread a little so they would stay kind of firm when you pick them up
This dish is one our family favorites! Great for evenings when time is of the essence. We serve the filling on low carb tortillas with Mexican blend cheese and guacamole. Delicious!
Great recipe love it will make it again.

My Family and I were looking for chicken Phillies and stumbled across this recipe. IT IS DELICIOUS!!. Instead of putting the salsa on the bread I added it to the chicken/veggie mixture and let it all cook together with the tomato juice. Also for added fajita flavor I picked up “fajita spice” from my local grocery store.
this was easy to make and oh so delicious
Made it twice. Toasted bread is the key. Used V8 juice because that’s what I had. Avocado was good to use.

I made this according to the recipe except for 2 things which I changed.
I added a little more Taco Seasoning and I did not use it over bread. I used it as a layered Nacho dish with a little cheese.
it was A HIT at the table.
we will be making more of this again!
thank you for the recipe!
